notes: Summary: evaluating Redwood Dedicated for latency-sensitive trading signals and reranking pipeline. Primary ask is a contractual throughput guarantee (min tokens/sec) plus predictable concurrency caps and a defined burst policy.

Client quoted targets during 02/24 demo: 40k tokens/sec sustained across 8k concurrent short requests (avg 5-12 tokens each) for reranking, and 6k tokens/sec with 512-token context for chat-style model used by trading desk.
Requested reserved GPU planning: initial commitment of 16 A100-equivalent GPUs for Q3 rollout, with option to scale +8 GPUs for peak season. Wants explicit pre-warm window for new reserved capacity.

Throughput guarantee asks (negotiation points): min_tokens_per_sec per tenant (global): 40,000; per-instance concurrency cap: 2,000; global concurrency safety cap: 10,000; burst allowance: 2x sustained for up to 10 minutes with automatic throttling afterwards.

Burst policy detail requested by customer: soft burst (token-limiter) + hard cap. They want SLA credit if sustained burst throttling occurs more than twice/month. Also want ability to route to cheaper model variants for surplus traffic automatically.

Latency SLOs: P95 < 120ms for 1-16 token responses (reranking path); P99 < 350ms for up to 512-token responses (chat path) when within reserved capacity. Redwood to provide per-route latency dashboards and sampling traces.

Cost sensitivity: high. Procurement expects blended unit cost below $0.0009/token given reserved commit and quantization recommendations from Redwood Optimize. They asked for a model of cost vs. reserved GPU count.
Security: must support VPC peering + customer-managed KMS, audit logs forwarded to Splunk. Data residency for EU subset of clients required; plan to push EU traffic to a regional Dedicated pool.
Technical concerns raised: KV cache warmup after scaling leading to 20-30% cost spike in POC. SE (Priya) proposed KV pre-warm strategy + prefix caching and a plan to instrument cache hit metrics.

Quote from Head of Platform (call 02/24): "We need hard guarantees for sustained throughput — bursts are fine but cannot be relied upon for trading signals." — framing requirement for contractual minima.
Proposed commercial structure: 12-month reserved capacity with quarterly true-ups, SLA credit schedule for missed tokens/sec targets, and optional burst pool billed as overage at agreed rate.

POC plan: run 48-hour perf sweep with representative workload (mix: 65% reranking short calls, 35% chat/512 tokens) on dedicated staging pool week of 2026-03-14. Customer will provide sample request traces and cost model.

Action items: (1) Redwood infra to produce proposal with min_tokens/sec per GPU and per-pool numbers + burst algorithm; (2) legal to draft SLA appendix language; (3) schedule 48-hour perf sweep and supply synthetic + replay traces.
Stubs/refs: pricing deck link in Drive; perf logs attached. Jira INF-4821 for KV-cache warmup investigation.
Tone: pragmatic but strict on guarantees. Procurement pushed for clearer penalties and rollback path if performance not met during onboarding.
